content: Melvin-Koushki reads Ibn Turka as contesting Āmulī: lettrism is hardly a subset of Sufism but encompasses both it and philosophy, though Sufism is a science in its own right and superior to the other Islamic sciences. He adds that Ibn Turka's sharp distinction between theoretical and practical lettrism and his championing of the former seems directly informed by Āmulī's recognition of a sīmiyāʾ/ʿilm al-ḥurūf binary.
